entries.claim: The "still mine" mtime check is a non-atomic check-then-rewrite, so a losing writer can rewind or delete the sidecar of a newly acquired claim.
entries.failure_scenario: Writer A loses an old claim, records its prior `found` mtime, stamps the sidecar, and reaches `statSync(dated).mtimeMs === mine`. Before A executes `utimesSync` (or `unlinkSync` when `found === null`), the old claimant completes and removes its claim, and writer B creates a new claim at the same paths and stamps its sidecar. A then restores/deletes B's sidecar based on its stale check. The fresh live claim now appears as old (or sidecar-less), allowing another rotation attempt to reclaim it while B is still rotating, risking concurrent rotation and trace corruption. Thus the original abandoned-claim clock issue is addressed in the uncontended losing case, but this fix introduces an unsafe concurrent-claim race.
